172.title: Import caller context: request fields and API examples

172.summary: Import customer-supplied context for callers on one account-owned business number. Each row merges supplied fields into that caller’s saved record; omitted fields stay unchanged.

caller_number.description: Caller identifier. Use E.164. Whitespace is removed and + is added when missing; the route does not enforce a numeric length limit.

name.description: Up to 120 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value.

email.description: Up to 120 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value. Nonempty email must have a local part, @, domain and dot.

phone.description: Up to 40 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value.

location.description: Up to 120 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value.

reference_id.description: Up to 64 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value.

preference.description: Up to 200 characters after conversion to text and trimming. Null clears; empty text is ignored; omitted keeps the saved value.

items.description: At least one supplied or cleared context field is required. Fields last_call and open_item are engine-only.

callers.description: Caller rows to validate and then write in order.

imported.description: Number of rows written, not unique callers.

172.retry: There is no documented idempotency-key replay guarantee. After a database error or timeout, read the affected caller records before a deliberate retry: some rows may already be saved. A repeat can overwrite newer context. Disable automatic write retries.

174.notes:
The endpoint has no dry-run mode. Only send to an authorised recipient. Do not infer a sender from agent settings, and do not send API credentials to a browser. The response can gain receipt fields when that feature is enabled; older successful responses contain only status, to and from.

An accepted message can still return 201 if later local history persistence fails. A receipt-path failure can include outcome, work_id, message_id and safe_to_retry both alongside the error and inside details. Do not infer not-sent from a generic 500 response.

174.summary: Send one SMS using an explicit sender owned by the account and assigned to the requested agent. A 201 sent response means the send was accepted; it is not proof of delivery to the recipient.

from_number.description: Explicit owned, settled sender assigned to this agent. There is no agent-number fallback.

to.description: Recipient number. This field is to, not to_number.

message.description: Nonempty text. This route declares no fixed character cap; encoding, segmentation and connection limits still apply.

reply_context.description: Optional instructions for a later reply context.

context.description: Optional JSON context saved with the accepted outbound message.

recipient_timezone.description: Optional recipient IANA time zone for contact checks.

status.description: Accepted send state; not a delivery receipt.

message_id.description: Optional accepted message identity when account receipts are enabled.

persistence.description: Optional persistence state returned by the receipt path.

safe_to_retry.description: False when supplied; do not resend an accepted message.

174.retry: Never automatically retry an SMS write. Preserve the accepted message/work IDs where available. If a timeout, connection failure or sms_outcome_unknown occurs, inspect receipts/history before deliberately sending again. An error’s retry hint does not override the no-automatic-write-retry rule.
